newsitem.title: MEXICO: Brother of Mexican finance minister killed.
newsitem.headline: Brother of Mexican finance minister killed.

text.p: The brother of Mexico's finance minister was gunned down on Saturday evening near his house in an upscale part of the city, officials said.
Alejandro Ortiz Martinez, brother of Mexico's Finance Minister Guillermo Ortiz, died after being hit by three bullets.
The director of the Mexican Judicial Police in the capital district, Luios Roberto Gutierrez Flores, told reporters the victim was the brother of the federal finance minister.
Government news agency Notimex said three gunmen fired on Ortiz Martinez, killing him in his late-model Mercedes-Benz as he got out of the vehicle after parking it in his driveway.
Television broadcasts showed a chaotic scene at the house in the posh Lomas de Chapultepec neighborhood. Police experts could be seen checking bullet holes in the car.
Gutierrez Flores said the crime appeared to be a robbery attempt, a common crime in Mexico City.
But a worker employed at the victim's house said the crime did not appear to be a robbery. "They did not assault him, only shot him," Leonardo Sanchez told radio reporters.
Finance Ministry officials were unavailable to comment.
Earlier on Saturday, a government budget director, Jorge Banuelos Orta, 51, was clubbed to death and stuffed into the trunk of his own car, the attorney-general's office for the capital said.
The body was found in the central Roma district of the city.
The shooting of the finance minister's brother would be the second killing of someone tied to the Mexican finance ministry in the last few weeks.
On July 13 a finance ministry official was killed after a high-speed car chase through the streets of the capital.
Section Director Pedro Jose Alvarez Porras was gunned down while driving with his wife through Mexico City.
